name: @media-router/plugin-video-player
description: Video player — MPEG-TS input rendered to a DRM/HDMI display

mediaRouter.description: Decodes an MPEG-TS video stream and renders it to a display via DRM/KMS

fallbackText.description: Overlay text when no stream is connected

fallbackImagePath.description: Image shown as fallback when no stream (otherwise SMPTE colour bars).

bufferMs.description: Pre-decode buffer. Keep low (200) for live SRT/RIST; raise (e.g. 1500) for HLS so the decoder has lookahead until the next I-frame after a mid-stream join. Adds end-to-end latency.

qos.description: Sink QoS. When ON (default), the sink can ask the decoder to drop frames if it falls behind — right for live SRT/RIST where keeping up matters more than completeness. Turn OFF for HLS so every decoded frame is presented; pairs with a larger bufferMs.

sync.description: Smooth playback vs lowest latency. ON (default): each frame is presented at its timestamp, giving smooth, evenly-paced playback — network and decode jitter is absorbed by letting early frames wait a few tens of ms (median added latency is ~zero). OFF: every frame is shown the instant it is ready — the lowest possible latency, at the cost of visible judder under jitter. Turn OFF for ultra-low-latency chains, or as the robust fallback for degraded sources with broken PCR timing, which can stall under paced playback.

clockSync.description: EXPERIMENTAL — known issue: freezes on the first frame (source-epoch vs shared-clock mismatch, see docs/TodoNotes-video-hw-decode.md). Intended purpose: lock to the shared engine clock so video stays in lipsync with an audio-decoder fed from the same source, when one stream is split into separate video + audio playout (pairs with lipSyncMs; requires the matching audio-decoder). Leave OFF until the epoch latch is wired in — the default Honour-buffer-PTS pacing covers everything except cross-pipeline lipsync.

lipSyncMs.description: Lip-sync trim. Positive DELAYS video to meet audio that's playing late (the audio path usually carries more buffering latency); negative advances it. Adjust live while watching until lips match. Only applies with Clock sync (or Sync) on.

cpuDecodeThreading.description: Software (CPU) decode threading — only matters when there's no GPU/VAAPI hardware decoder. AUTO (default): one core, zero added latency — right for live. But a heavy 4K stream can max that core and drop frames. MULTI-CORE: spreads the decode across all CPU cores so 4K keeps up, at the cost of ~130–160 ms added latency (it decodes several frames ahead). Turn this ON only when the CPU genuinely can't keep up AND you can spend the latency — otherwise leave it on AUTO for low-latency live.
